LinkedIn B2B engagement is generally reported best on weekday mornings (e.g. Tue-Thu) rather than every single day including weekends -- not assuming that for you, just flagging it's worth a look before this goes live. Change the cron expression to whatever cadence/days you actually want.

nodes.name: Get All Posts
nodes.notes: TODO(Alan): create a Sheet named 'Posts' with columns: postText, imageFileId (optional -- Google Drive file ID of the image, leave blank for a text-only post), scheduledDate (YYYY-MM-DD), status (pending/posted/failed), postId, postUrl. Reuse the same Google Sheets credential already wired into the YouTube workflow -- don't create a second one. This reads every row every run; filtering to only the ones ready to post happens in the next node.

nodes.name: Filter Ready To Post
nodes.notes: Known n8n import quirk: this Filter node's Value fields sometimes need to be re-typed by hand in the UI even when the JSON looks correct -- open the node and confirm both conditions are actually populated before relying on it. Also verify how Google Sheets is actually returning scheduledDate (string vs. serial date) -- the JS Date() parsing above assumes a plain YYYY-MM-DD string; adjust if the Sheet gives something else.

nodes.name: Download Image File
nodes.notes: Reuse the same Google Drive credential already wired into the YouTube workflow. Alan pastes the image's Drive file ID directly into the Sheet row -- no separate 'Pending' folder or filename-matching step like YouTube's, since here the Sheet row (not a dropped file) is what triggers the post. Flagging this as a deliberate deviation from the YouTube pattern, not a silent one -- YouTube's video file arrival IS the event; here the post is scheduled by date in the Sheet and the image is just optional metadata on that row.

nodes.name: Update Row Status
nodes.notes: Matches by row_number (n8n's Google Sheets node exposes this automatically on read) rather than a content column, since postText could repeat across rows and there's no other guaranteed-unique column. postUrl format is a guess (LinkedIn's actual share/post URL shape for organization posts) -- verify and correct once a real post succeeds.

nodes.name: Notify Success (Gmail Draft)

parameters.subject: ={{ 'LinkedIn post succeeded' }}
parameters.message: ={{ 'Post text: ' + $('Filter Ready To Post').item.json.postText + '\nScheduled for: ' + $('Filter Ready To Post').item.json.scheduledDate + '\nURL: https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/' + $json.id }}

nodes.notes: Matches the Gmail-draft notification pattern already used by content-log.md / prospecting-log.md / RingCentral / YouTube. Fires on every successful auto-publish so there's a record without checking LinkedIn daily.

nodes.name: Notify Failure (Gmail Draft)

parameters.subject: ={{ 'LinkedIn post FAILED: ' + ($json.postText || '').substring(0, 60) }}
parameters.message:
={{ 'Post text: ' + $json.postText + '
Scheduled for: ' + $json.scheduledDate + '
Error: ' + JSON.stringify($json.errorBody) + '

Row status was NOT updated, so it will retry next run. If the error is something that will never succeed (e.g. bad image file), fix or clear the row yourself or it will keep failing and notifying every run.' }}

nodes.notes: TODO(Alan): decide if repeated-failure rows should auto-flip to status=failed after N retries instead of notifying forever, same open question as the YouTube workflow. Not built -- flagging rather than guessing your tolerance for noise.
